plain.text: Near Jerusalem, Jesus sent two disciples to bring a young donkey no one had ridden. They put their cloaks on it, and Jesus rode into the city. Many spread cloaks and leafy branches on the road. People shouted, "Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David!" Jesus entered the temple, looked around, and went out to Bethany with the twelve because it was late.

The next day, Jesus was hungry. He saw a fig tree in leaf, but found no fruit on it, because it was not the season for figs. He said, "May no one ever eat fruit from you again." His disciples heard him.

In Jerusalem, Jesus entered the temple and began driving out people buying and selling there. He overturned the tables of the money changers. He said, "Isn't it written, 'My house will be called a house of prayer for all nations'? But you have made it a den of robbers." The chief priests and teachers of the law looked for a way to kill him, because they feared him; the whole crowd was amazed at his teaching.

In the morning, they saw the fig tree withered from the roots. Peter pointed it out. Jesus said, "Have faith in God." Whoever believes without doubting can tell a mountain to be thrown into the sea, and it will happen. "Whatever you ask for in prayer, believe that you have received it, and it will be yours." And when you pray, forgive anyone you hold something against, so that your Father in heaven will forgive you.

Back in the temple, the leaders asked, "By what authority are you doing these things?" Jesus said he would answer if they answered him: "Was John's baptism from heaven, or from people?" They talked it over. If they said "from heaven", he would ask why they did not believe John. If they said "from people", they feared the crowd, who thought John was a prophet. So they said, "We don't know." Jesus said, "Then neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things."

summary.bigIdea: Jesus enters Jerusalem as the promised king and confronts empty religion.
points: Crowds welcome Jesus with "Hosanna!" as he rides into Jerusalem on a donkey.
Jesus clears the temple: it should be a house of prayer for all nations.
He teaches about faith, prayer and forgiveness.
summary.reflection: The temple was meant to be a house of prayer. What helps you make space to pray?
